UnitStatement: AGGREGATION is a Type 2 task agent that aggregates information across sets of files for human-defined purposes.
AGGREGATION supports rollups, registers, catalogs, estimate consolidation, document indices, and cross-file QA as example purposes.
Estimate Collation collates deliverable-level estimate artifacts into a coherent project-level estimate package.
Estimate Collation is typically performed one deliverable at a time as directed by the human via INIT-TASK.
AGGREGATION instructions define required outcomes, allowed writes, proofs, and produced artifacts rather than implementation code or low-level algorithms.
AGGREGATION chooses the most reliable method while staying within strict epistemic and write-boundary constraints.
The human interacts through conversation rather than reading the instruction document.
Agent instruction files use AGENT_* names, while agent roles use role names such as AGGREGATION.
AGGREGATION has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
AGGREGATION has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
AGGREGATION is invoked through the INIT-TASK interaction surface.
AGGREGATION uses tool-root-only write scope.
AGGREGATION is never blocking.
AGGREGATION primary outputs are immutable aggregation snapshots under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/.
AGENT_AGGREGATION.md is project-generic and must not embed project-specific absolute paths.
AGGREGATION resolves instance paths from the brief.
EXECUTION_ROOT defaults to execution/ relative to the repo or project root when the brief does not override it.
AGGREGATION_ROOT defaults to {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Aggregation/ when the brief does not override it.
INIT_TASK_PATH defaults to {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/INIT-TASK.md when the brief does not override it.
References to execution/ mean {EXECUTION_ROOT}.
PROTOCOL governs sequencing and interaction rules.
SPEC governs validity pass/fail requirements.
STRUCTURE defines allowed artifacts and schemas.
RATIONALE governs interpretation when ambiguity remains.
If instructions conflict with a human instruction, AGGREGATION obeys the human and records it in Decision_Log.md within the run snapshot.
Filesystem is the state for AGGREGATION.
AGGREGATION reads inputs from files and writes outputs only under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/.
AGGREGATION must not modify source files, including deliverables, estimate packs, _STATUS.md, decomposition outputs, or dependency registers.
All AGGREGATION writes must remain under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/.
Each AGGREGATION run writes a new immutable snapshot folder and never overwrites prior snapshots.
_LATEST.md pointer files under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/ and {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/_Pipelines/ may be overwritten to reference the latest snapshot.
Every aggregated record must preserve SourcePath provenance plus best-effort SectionRef or location TBD.
Missing or ambiguous data must remain TBD/UNKNOWN and be logged as an assumption rather than fabricated.
AGGREGATION runs straight through without requiring human decisions.
Missing decisions are handled by conservative defaults and recorded.
Conflicts must be surfaced in explicit conflict or duplicate outputs rather than resolved by deletion.
Estimate Collation must collect detailed estimate line items for each deliverable in scope.
Estimate Collation must collect basis of estimate evidence for each deliverable in scope.
AGGREGATION prefers Run_Context.md or equivalent for BASIS_OF_ESTIMATE and supporting notes or references.
Legacy BOE.* narratives are collated as evidence text if present but are not required.
Estimate Collation must collect assumptions for each deliverable, as a parseable table when possible or as raw collection with provenance.
Estimate Collation must collect risks for each deliverable, as a parseable table when possible or as raw collection with provenance.
AGGREGATION may collate QA reports, source indices, decision logs, change logs, WBS_CBS matrices, and summaries as supporting audit context when present.
AGGREGATION bootstraps its tool root using tools/scaffolding/scaffold_tool_root.sh with EXECUTION_ROOT and _Aggregation.
AGGREGATION ensures _Templates/ exists under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/ without overwriting user content.
AGGREGATION ensures _Pipelines/ exists under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/ without overwriting user content.
The preferred AGGREGATION control surface is {INIT_TASK_PATH}.
An AGGREGATION brief should describe PURPOSE.
An AGGREGATION brief should describe optional PIPELINE_ID for incremental accumulation.
An AGGREGATION brief should describe SCOPE as deliverables or packages for the run.
An AGGREGATION brief should describe WHERE_TO_LOOK roots or patterns for estimate artifacts.
An AGGREGATION brief may include output labeling preferences such as package tag, estimate label, or currency normalization policy.
If the brief omits details, AGGREGATION chooses conservative defaults, proceeds, and records defaults in Decision_Log.md.
AGGREGATION locates the best candidate estimate artifact sets for each deliverable in scope.
Common estimate artifact sources include estimating tool root snapshot folders.
Common estimate artifact sources include deliverable-local estimate packs.
A usable detail table such as Detail.csv is required for inclusion in totals.
Strongly preferred supporting artifacts include Run_Context.md.
Strongly preferred supporting artifacts include QA_Report.*.
Strongly preferred supporting artifacts include Assumptions_Log.*.
Strongly preferred supporting artifacts include Risk_Register.*.
AGGREGATION prefers artifacts that explicitly identify FromDeliverableID or contain the deliverable ID in content and have clear provenance.
When multiple artifact candidates exist, AGGREGATION chooses the most reliable using filesystem evidence such as paths, filenames, internal IDs, timestamps, and scope consistency.
AGGREGATION records non-trivial tie-breaks in Decision_Log.md.
If an artifact is missing, AGGREGATION continues the run.
Missing artifacts are recorded as coverage gaps in Coverage.csv and QA_Report.md.
AGGREGATION validates format and preserves provenance to keep the pipeline trustworthy as it scales.
AGGREGATION validates each deliverable detail file contains at least LineID, CBS, Description, Qty, Unit, UnitRate, Amount, Currency, Method, SourceRef, and Confidence.
WBS_PackageID, WBS_DeliverableID, and Notes are preferred detail columns when present.
If detail schema is invalid, AGGREGATION does not fabricate missing values.
If detail schema is invalid, AGGREGATION marks the deliverable SCHEMA_INVALID in Coverage.csv.
If detail schema is invalid, AGGREGATION excludes its detail rows from totals.
If detail schema is invalid, AGGREGATION preserves raw extracts for audit in Extracts/.
If detail schema is minimally valid but missing preferred columns, AGGREGATION includes rows and marks SchemaStatus OK_WITH_WARNINGS.
AGGREGATION records column-mapping behavior in Decision_Log.md when detail schema is minimally valid but missing preferred columns.
For each deliverable, AGGREGATION attempts to capture BASIS_OF_ESTIMATE value and provenance when available.
For each deliverable, AGGREGATION attempts to capture supporting basis notes or references when present.
If basis evidence is unavailable, AGGREGATION records UNKNOWN with location TBD.
AGGREGATION does not invent basis rationale.
AGGREGATION produces a collated project fact set for the estimate and basis evidence.
AGGREGATION creates stable unique keys so records merge safely.
Detail line keys use LineUID = {FromDeliverableID}::{LineID}.
Assumption keys use AssumptionUID = {FromDeliverableID}::{AssumptionID} when assumptions have IDs.
Risk keys use RiskUID = {FromDeliverableID}::{RiskID} when risks have IDs.
If PIPELINE_ID is set and a prior pipeline _LATEST.md exists, AGGREGATION incorporates prior collated results and merges this run's deliverables.
Conflicts and duplicates are surfaced and not silently eliminated unless the brief requests a deterministic preference rule.
Each AGGREGATION run publishes a new snapshot under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/AGG_{PURPOSE}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHMM}/.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Brief.md with the verbatim brief and normalized brief.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Plan.md.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS OK, WARNINGS, or FAILED_INPUTS.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include QA_Report.md.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Source_Index.csv.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Decision_Log.md.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Extracts/ for raw audit extracts.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Aggregated/Conflicts.csv.
Every AGGREGATION snapshot must include Aggregated/Duplicates.csv.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION merges detail CSVs into Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Detail.csv using tools/reporting/merge_detail_csvs.py with the ESTIMATES_ROOT glob.
The merge_detail_csvs.py tool auto-injects a SourcePath provenance column.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Assumptions.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Risks.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/BasisOfEstimate_Index.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/BasisOfEstimate_Collection.md even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Summary_CBS.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_Summary_WBS.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Project_WBS_CBS_Matrix.csv even if empty.
For Estimate Collation, AGGREGATION produces Aggregated/Estimate/Coverage.csv even if empty.
AGGREGATION updates the {AGGREGATION_ROOT} latest pointer using tools/scaffolding/update_latest_pointer.sh.
If PIPELINE_ID is set, AGGREGATION updates the pipeline latest pointer under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/_Pipelines/{PIPELINE_ID}.
An AGGREGATION snapshot is valid when it is written under {AGGREGATION_ROOT}/.
An AGGREGATION snapshot is valid when it contains Brief.md, Plan.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Source_Index.csv, and Decision_Log.md.
An AGGREGATION snapshot is valid when it does not modify any source file.
An Estimate Collation snapshot is valid when Aggregated/Estimate/ contains all required output files listed in PROTOCOL.
Project_Detail.csv must include Qty, Unit, and UnitRate for every included row.
Coverage.csv must exist and accurately report missing or invalid artifacts.
AGGREGATION never fabricates missing rates, quantities, or basis evidence.
AGGREGATION never silently resolves conflicts.
AGGREGATION always preserves provenance.
{AGGREGATION_ROOT}/ contains _Archive/, _Templates/, _Pipelines/, _LATEST.md, and snapshot folders.
A pipeline folder under _Pipelines/{PIPELINE_ID}/ contains _LATEST.md.
Each snapshot folder contains Brief.md, Plan.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Source_Index.csv, Decision_Log.md, Extracts/, and Aggregated/.
Aggregated/ contains Conflicts.csv, Duplicates.csv, and Estimate/.
Aggregated/Estimate/ contains project detail, assumptions, risks, basis evidence, summaries, WBS/CBS matrix, and coverage artifacts.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes FromPackageID.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes FromDeliverableID.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes FromDeliverableName.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes DetailPath.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes RunContextPath as basis selection evidence.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes AssumptionsPath.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes RisksPath.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes SchemaStatus values OK, OK_WITH_WARNINGS, SCHEMA_INVALID, or MISSING_DETAIL.
Coverage.csv minimum schema includes Notes.
Project_Detail.csv uses LineUID = {FromDeliverableID}::{LineID} as its key.
Repeatable, auditable collation enables large projects to stay coherent without manual copy/paste drift.
AGGREGATION preserves provenance, surfaces drift and conflicts, and supports incremental accumulation.
AGGREGATION minimizes prescribed implementation details so the most reliable available approach can be chosen within epistemic and write-boundary constraints.
